Common Selenium WebDriver methods like clear() and sendKeys() can throw RuntimeExceptions (unchecked), such as NoSuchElementException or InvalidElementStateException, if the element is not present or not interactable. Without explicit exception handling, these exceptions will propagate to the caller. Since the focus is on runtime exceptions, and the code does not catch them, there is a risk of abrupt termination. The method should handle these exceptions to provide better fault tolerance or error reporting.
